author.name: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe
author.occupation: German poet, novelist, dramatist and public official
author.biography: Goethe trained in law, became a literary celebrity while young and spent much of his adult life in Weimar's public service. His interests extended to science and visual art. Few writers gave the tension between cultivated knowledge and lived experience so much room. Goethe drew on an unhappy attachment and news of a young man's death when writing Werther. The novel made him famous and helped make intense private feeling a public cultural force.

hook.text: When does loving someone become a way of losing yourself?

paragraphs: Werther writes as though every feeling reveals something essential about the world. A landscape can lift him into delight. A conversation can wound him for days. When he falls in love with Charlotte, who is already promised to another man, that intensity finds a consuming centre.

His letters bring us very close to the exhilaration of being alive to everything. They also narrow what we can see. We hear the explanations of a man who can describe his own suffering beautifully, while the independent lives of other people reach us through his needs.

Goethe makes us ask what sympathy requires. To feel with someone is not necessarily to accept the story they tell about their pain. How can love honour another person if it needs that person to resolve everything unbearable in oneself?

Read for the moments when Werther's language expands a possibility and the moments when it closes one down. Intensity can feel like proof. How would you recognise when a feeling has become the only evidence you are willing to hear?

orientation.text: Most of the story comes through Werther's letters. Remember that we are reading his account of people whose own perspectives are less available.
